findings.title: Stray `if` in `<%- end if %>` corrupts the compiled template
findings.body: The closing tag of the header conditional is written as `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The extra `if` is compiled into Ruby as `end if <next emitted expression>`, i.e. the whole if/else block becomes the body of a modifier-`if` whose condition is whatever ERB happens to emit next (currently a whitespace `safe_append`). At best this works by accident and the header is rendered conditionally on an unrelated expression; a small change to surrounding whitespace/markup can turn it into a SyntaxError raised while rendering the embed page. Nothing catches this because controller specs do not render views (`render_views` is not enabled in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb).

findings.title: Feed HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)
findings.body: `poll_feed` takes `i.content`, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML` on it (turning escaped markup back into live HTML) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb:133) then returns `raw` verbatim, so the feed HTML is stored in `cooked` with no sanitization and is later emitted with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19) and by the normal topic rendering. Any `<script>`, `onerror=`, or `javascript:` payload in the polled feed becomes persistent script execution on the forum for every visitor. The content should be run through the same whitelist/sanitizer used for `import_remote` (and `javascript:` hrefs stripped) before being trusted as raw HTML.

findings.title: poll_feed crashes on feed items without `content`
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item exposes a non-nil `content`. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom `content` / `content:encoded`), so `i.content` is nil and the job raises NoMethodError. Because the job is declared with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll aborts on the first such item and every remaining item in the feed is silently dropped. The same applies to `i.title`, which `TopicEmbed.import` passes to `PostCreator` as the topic title.

findings.title: Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of an embed URL
findings.body: `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies, the Redis connection drops, or the EXPIRE command fails between the two calls, the throttle key is left with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` will return true forever for that embed URL, so the topic for that URL can never be retrieved again (the embed page will loop on the loading screen indefinitely). Use a single atomic command, e.g. `$redis.set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: `href.start_with?('/')` is also true for protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The rewrite then strips all leading slashes (`sub(/^\/+/, '')`) and prefixes the embed host, turning `//cdn.example.com/img.png` into `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/img.png`, i.e. working absolute links/images in imported articles become broken links. The same bug applies to the `img` loop at lines 68-73. Protocol-relative URLs should be left alone (or only given a scheme), and relative URLs without a leading slash (`images/x.png`) are not handled at all — `URI.join` would handle all of these cases correctly.

findings.title: TopicEmbed created from a post that may not have been saved; unique-index race unhandled
findings.body: `creator.create` returns the (possibly unsaved) Post instance even when creation failed — PostCreator rolls back and returns `@post` carrying errors — so `post.present?` is true while `post.id` and `post.topic_id` are nil. `TopicEmbed.create!` then violates the NOT NULL constraints on `topic_id`/`post_id` and raises inside the job instead of failing gracefully; use `post.persisted?`. Additionally, `embed_url` has a unique index (db/migrate/20131217174004), and two concurrent retrievals for the same URL (the existence check in TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve is a plain read) will make one of them blow up with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique; that case should be rescued and treated as "already imported".

findings.title: `import` mutates the caller's contents string
findings.body: `contents << "...imported_from..."` appends to the string object passed in by the caller rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse the string (or pass a frozen/literal string, which raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`) get surprising behaviour, and calling `import` twice with the same object appends the footer twice. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

findings.title: request.referer interpolated into a JS string literal and used as postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects a client-controlled header into inline JavaScript. ERB's HTML escaping does not apply to characters that matter inside a `<script>` block (a backslash is not escaped, and escaped entities are not decoded inside script elements), so a crafted Referer can break the surrounding string literal and produce a JS syntax error, and the full referer URL (path, query) is used where only an origin is meaningful. Derive the target origin from the validated host instead, e.g. `"#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}"` built from the parsed referer and JSON/JS-escaped.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin happens to be a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` instead of comparing origins for equality. This is fragile (e.g. a configured URL containing a path or a longer host can make unintended origins match) and silently accepts messages that should be rejected, letting a third party resize the frame. Compare `e.origin` against the exact origin parsed out of `discourseUrl`.

findings.title: New embed.css / embed.js assets are not added to the precompile list
findings.body: The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the whole feature depends on third-party sites loading `embed.js` directly, but neither `embed.css` nor `embed.js` is a Sprockets entry point reachable from `application.js`/`application.css`, and this PR does not add them to `config.assets.precompile` (config/application.rb is untouched). In production with asset digests/compilation this raises `Asset was not declared to be precompiled in production` when the embed page is rendered and `embed.js` will 404 for embedding sites.

findings.title: "is 404 without an embed_url" passes for the wrong reason
findings.body: This example does not stub `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so the `ensure_embeddable` before_filter raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess('embeddable host not set')` before `params.require(:embed_url)` is ever reached. The test therefore asserts nothing about the missing-parameter behaviour (and would keep passing if `params.require` were removed). It should stub `embeddable_host` and a matching referer, and assert the actual expected status. There is also no example covering a referer whose host differs from `embeddable_host` — the main security check of this controller.

findings.title: PollFeed guard examples are tautological and poll_feed itself is untested
findings.body: `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to false, so the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples would pass even if those two conditions were removed from `execute`; they need `feed_polling_enabled?` stubbed true and only the setting under test blanked. More importantly, `poll_feed` — the part that fetches the feed, picks `i.link`/`i.id`, unescapes content and calls `TopicEmbed.import` — has no coverage at all, which is why the nil-`content` crash and the unsanitized-HTML path are unguarded.

findings.title: Already-shipped migration edited to add `force: true`
findings.body: Adding `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics` changes an existing, already-released migration so that it silently drops the `top_topics` table if it exists. Anyone re-running this migration (e.g. after a schema_migrations reset or a partial rollback) now loses the table and its data instead of getting a clear "table already exists" error. This change is also unrelated to the embedding feature in this PR.

findings.title: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid header value
findings.body: `ALLOWALL` is not a defined X-Frame-Options directive. Browser handling of unknown values varies: some ignore the header entirely (which is the intent, but only by accident), others treat an unparseable value conservatively and refuse to frame the page, which would break embedding. To allow framing, the header should simply not be emitted (delete it) rather than set to an invalid token.

findings.title: Kernel#open used for remote fetching (no timeout/size limit, pipe/file handling)
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` use `Kernel#open` from open-uri, which interprets a leading `|` as a shell command and happily opens local file paths, and imposes no read timeout or response size limit. The whole response is read into memory inside a Sidekiq job. Use `URI.parse` plus an explicit HTTP client (or at minimum validate the scheme is http/https and cap the read) so a mistyped/hostile setting or feed link cannot execute a command, read local files, or hang/OOM the worker.

findings.title: Only the Rails 4 lockfile was updated for the new gems
findings.body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added to the Gemfile and recorded in `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, but the Rails 3 lockfile (used when booting with `RAILS3=1`, see the dual-boot logic at the top of this Gemfile) was not regenerated. Booting/deploying in Rails 3 mode with a frozen or `--deployment` bundle will fail because the lockfile no longer matches the Gemfile.
